today.code: # 1. STT: WebSocket session stt = STTSession(model=STT, sample_rate=16_000) await stt.connect() # 2. Model: HTTP stream, split into sentences stream = client.chat.completions.create( model=LLM, stream=True, tools=TOOLS, ...) # 3. TTS: raw WebSocket, no SDK tts = TTSSession(model=TTS, voice="af_alloy") # then you write: real-time pacing, end-of-turn, # sentence splitting, the tool loop, barge-in with # context.cancel, reconnects, 16 kHz in / 24 kHz out

proposed.code: session = client.realtime.voice( stt=STT, model=LLM, tts=TTS, voice="af_alloy", turn_detection={"type": "semantic"}, tools=TOOLS, ) async for event in session.run(mic): if event.type == "response.audio.delta": speaker.play(event.audio) # barge-in handled in the session; # session.cancel() when you need it

footnote: 20 turns per row, synthetic speech, one region, measured client-side. One default model per stage; model choice is not the point here
